title: Super Howe duality and rigidity of hybrid Fourier transforms
authors: Jing-Song Huang, Yongzhi Luan, Yinuo Xue
abstract: We characterize the hybrid Fourier transform on the Schwartz--Grassmann space $\caS(\bbR^m)\otimesΛ_{2n}$ by operator intertwining relations. Using the bosonic oscillator Howe decomposition and the fermionic Lefschetz decomposition, we describe the action of the hybrid Fourier transform on both tensor factors. We show that first-order covariance with respect to coordinate multiplication and differentiation determines the transform up to a scalar. For $m,n\ge1$, we prove that covariance under all even quadratic operators, together with any one nonzero mixed quadratic operator, determines the linear span of the hybrid Fourier transform and its inverse. This rigidity result is obtained by computing the ordinary commutants of the even and full quadratic oscillator actions of $\fosp(4n|2m)$. After a degree-scaling change of normalization, we make the hybrid Fourier transform unitary with respect to the occupation number inner product, and factor it into a bosonic oscillator rotation and (up to a scalar phase) an $SU(2)$ rotation in the fermionic Lefschetz representation. For $m=1$ and $n\ge2$, we show that full even quadratic covariance together with the parity-preserving cubic relation for $qQ_f$ determines the unitary transform up to a global phase and a fermion-parity phase. Finally we calculate the unitary conjugation formulas for Hubbard--Holstein Hamiltonian for a hybrid continuous-variable and discrete-variable quantum system.
summary: This paper rigorously characterizes the hybrid Fourier transform connecting bosonic and fermionic quantum systems using advanced techniques from representation theory. It establishes a strong rigidity result, showing that the transform is uniquely determined by its covariance properties. The work culminates in demonstrating that this transform unitarily diagonalizes and relates the spectrum of the physically relevant Hubbard–Holstein Hamiltonian.
main_problem: The paper characterizes the hybrid Fourier transform connecting continuous bosonic and discrete fermionic degrees of freedom, and proves its rigidity under various covariance conditions.
main_result: The hybrid Fourier transform is shown to be unitary and its structure is determined by covariance relations, leading to explicit formulas for its conjugation action on Hamiltonians.
method: The analysis employs representation theory, utilizing the bosonic oscillator Howe decomposition and the fermionic Lefschetz decomposition to study intertwining relations between operators.
model_or_system: The study focuses on hybrid quantum systems combining continuous bosonic variables (modeled by $S(\mathbb{R}^m)$) and fermionic variables ($\Lambda^{2n}$). A key application is the unitary conjugation of the Hubbard–Holstein Hamiltonian.
key_observables: The unitary transform $U_{\sigma}^{m|2n}$, the Hamiltonian $H$, and its transformed counterpart $U_{\sigma}^{1|2n}H(U_{\sigma}^{1|2n})^\dagger$.
important_parameters: The dimensions $m$ and $n$ (bosonic and fermionic degrees of freedom), and the coupling constants in the Hamiltonian.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the operator $T$ is continuous and complex-linear, and the rigidity results are proven for specific dimensional regimes ($m, n \ge 1$ or $m=1, n \ge 2$).
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by analyzing the structure of the transform on the bosonic and fermionic sectors separately using decomposition theorems, then combines these results to establish the rigidity of the full hybrid transform, culminating in the application to the Hubbard-Holstein Hamiltonian.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical framework for characterizing unitary transformations between different representations of interacting quantum systems, especially those bridging continuous and discrete variables, is highly relevant for quantum optics and many-body physics.
